sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Piano alone; the platform before anything happens.

sections.name: Look up
sections.description: The singer looks up and sees the first snow.

sections.name: Train
sections.description: The flake melts; the train arrives; a private smile.

linguistic_source.reading: ためいき かぞえて
linguistic_source.normalized_reading: ためいき かぞえて

linguistic_source.reading: おくれる でんしゃ
linguistic_source.normalized_reading: おくれる でんしゃ

song.premise: The year's first snow begins while someone waits on an open-air platform, and the small surprise loosens a worry they have carried all day.
song.narrator_stance: First person, half under the breath, not performing for anyone.
song.central_tension: A day's worry keeps the eyes on the ground; one flake asks them to look up without making a speech about it.
song.state_at_start: Head down, counting sighs, annoyed at a late train.
song.intended_destination: Looking up, noticing, and a small private smile as the train pulls in.
song.listener_after: Remembers the moment of looking up more than any words.
creative_invariants: Never name happiness or relief in the lyric; the change must be musical.
No Christmas signifiers, no big final chorus, no key change.
The look-up moment is the only place the register opens.

sections.intended_transition: Establish a low, closed piano colour.
sections.state_after: We are waiting with the singer.

sections.dramatic_function: Show the worry without explaining it.
sections.intended_transition: Low, narrow, late-entering lines that sink at their ends.
sections.state_after: Stuck on the ground, unresolved on the dominant.

sections.dramatic_function: The look-up: the only opening of register and texture.
sections.intended_transition: Enter on the downbeat, rise, breathe, then hold the flake.
The flake melts on the sleeve; texture thins as the train arrives.
sections.state_after: A small smile, resolved but light.

lyric_anchor.text: ふと見上げたら 白いひとひら

phrase_directions.purpose: Make the moment of looking up audible as a change of posture, not as a statement of feeling.
phrase_directions.subtext: The worry has not gone; it has just been interrupted by something small and white.
phrase_directions.intended_transition: From late, sinking entries to a downbeat entry that rises, catches a breath, and lands on a held focus word.
phrase_directions.state_after: Eyes up; attention on one flake.
phrase_directions.delivery_arc: Soft and breathy, opening up through the rise, then a brighter, held ひとひら with a short late vibrato.

realization_hypothesis.summary: Downbeat entry plus the first rising contour and register opening of the song, with ひとひら on quarter notes against the verse's eighths and a harmony voice joining only on the focus word.
realization_hypothesis.melody: Rise from D4 to B4 across ふと見上げたら; ひとひら peaks on A4.
realization_hypothesis.rhythm: Verse lines enter late on eighths; the anchor enters on beat one and lengthens to quarters on ひとひら.
realization_hypothesis.harmony: G then D/F# for the look-up, Em7 to A under the focus word, resolving later in the coda.
realization_hypothesis.register: Lead climbs above E4 for the first time.
realization_hypothesis.dynamics: DYN rises through the look-up and eases on the held flake.
realization_hypothesis.tuning: Opening arc widens on the rise; small scoop into the peak ひ; short vibrato on the final ら.
realization_hypothesis.arrangement_space: Bass, a light kit, and high piano 'flakes' enter only at the look-up.

listening_question.question: Can I hear the moment the singer looks up from the worry to the snow, without the song telling me in words that they feel better?

review_notes.observation: Listened to the final song and judged it good; the look-up moment works. Keep.
